answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each account to lock scarce tokens before it can post offers or vote, then slash that stake when independently verified fraud is proven. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up real capital, and detected cheating burns it rather than merely losing a disposable account. The lock also limits how quickly an attacker can flood the market. A pearl buyer, a relic appraiser, and an ocean-route planner all face the same costly entry rule.
